title: A Clean Slate for Offline Reinforcement Learning

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, 'Solution 2: Consistent Reimplementations and a Unified Algorithm' paragraph
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The claim that their implementations achieve 'average training speedups of 131.5× and 74.8× against OfflineRL-Kit [16] and CORL [17]' is not supported by any data in the paper.  Appendix F (Table 2) reports individual speedup factors that are all below 21×, and the maximum individual speedup against OfflineRL-Kit is 20.8× (CQL) and against CORL is 16.25× (IQL).  The claimed averages are impossible given these numbers.  Figure 5 also shows speedup values (4x–16x) that are far lower.  The paper thus misrepresents the magnitude of the speedup.

The text states that TD3-AWR 'underperforms or matches [ReBRAC] on others, such as pen-human and kitchen-mixed.'  However, Figure 6 and the full results in Appendix J (Figure 14) show that TD3-AWR clearly outperforms ReBRAC on pen-human-v1 (mean score ≈65–70 for TD3‑AWR vs ≈40 for ReBRAC), and it also slightly outperforms ReBRAC on kitchen-mixed-v0.  The statement is factually incorrect relative to the presented figures.

Section 5.2 claims 'Figure 7 shows how MoBRAC outperforms other model-based methods for all datasets, except for MOPO in maze2d-large-v1.'  Appendix K (Figure 15 caption and body) instead says 'MoBRAC outperforms the other model-based methods in 6 out of 9 datasets and is tied with MOPO for 3 others.'  The main text implies MOPO beats MoBRAC on maze2d-large-v1, while the appendix states that MoBRAC is tied with MOPO on that or other datasets.  These descriptions contradict each other.
